        Generated for scope 'lab'. Verified on a lab unit (8.10, 2026-10-12). It is the unit's whole IP Tables list, in the
        unit's order, from the scope's management permit list (tacctl scope mgmt-acl lab list; the global
        tacctl config mgmt-acl list when the scope has none), the tacctl server's address and the scope's
        SNMP clients (tacctl scope snmp lab clients list). Add one line per entry under /N, IP Tables,
        in this order. The number is the line's place in the list, not part of the command; a line that
        starts with # is a note for you. The final DROP is not in this list: it is the last step, below.

              # the unit's own traffic: loopback, and the replies to its own connections
           1. iptables -A INPUT -i lo -j ACCEPT
           2. iptables -A INPUT -m conntrack --ctstate ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT
              # the tacctl server 10.0.0.42/32: ssh and https
           3. iptables -A INPUT -p tcp -s 10.0.0.42/32 --dport 22 -j ACCEPT
           4. iptables -A INPUT -p tcp -s 10.0.0.42/32 --dport 443 -j ACCEPT
              # permitted range 192.0.2.0/24: ssh and https
           5. iptables -A INPUT -p tcp -s 192.0.2.0/24 --dport 22 -j ACCEPT
           6. iptables -A INPUT -p tcp -s 192.0.2.0/24 --dport 443 -j ACCEPT
              # SNMP (udp 161): the tacctl server, then the scope's SNMP clients
           7. iptables -A INPUT -p udp -s 10.0.0.42/32 --dport 161 -j ACCEPT
           8. iptables -A INPUT -p udp -s 203.0.113.0/24 --dport 161 -j ACCEPT
              # ICMP (ping) from the same networks, on eth0
           9. iptables -A INPUT -i eth0 -s 10.0.0.42/32 -p icmp -j ACCEPT
          10. iptables -A INPUT -i eth0 -s 192.0.2.0/24 -p icmp -j ACCEPT
          11. iptables -A INPUT -i eth0 -s 203.0.113.0/24 -p icmp -j ACCEPT

        The same rules in one paste, for the IP Tables prompt (/N, item 5): no comments, no DROP. The paste
        replaces every entry the unit holds, so read its list first ('>' and '<' page through it): what this
        list lacks is gone afterwards. The unit takes the block in one go ("Configuring iptables - Please
        wait..."), applies the rules at once and shows 'IP Tables: On' on the /N menu; any session that
        leaves a top-level menu saves the configuration, this paste included. The block is at the left
        margin on purpose: paste it as it is.

<iptables>
iptables -A INPUT -i lo -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -m conntrack --ctstate ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -p tcp -s 10.0.0.42/32 --dport 22 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -p tcp -s 10.0.0.42/32 --dport 443 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -p tcp -s 192.0.2.0/24 --dport 22 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -p tcp -s 192.0.2.0/24 --dport 443 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -p udp -s 10.0.0.42/32 --dport 161 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -p udp -s 203.0.113.0/24 --dport 161 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -i eth0 -s 10.0.0.42/32 -p icmp -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -i eth0 -s 192.0.2.0/24 -p icmp -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -i eth0 -s 203.0.113.0/24 -p icmp -j ACCEPT
</iptables>

        Notes on the list:
          - Line 2: older builds take '-m state --state ESTABLISHED,RELATED' in place of
            '-m conntrack --ctstate ESTABLISHED,RELATED'. It covers the replies of the unit's own TACACS+,
            RADIUS, DNS and NTP queries.
          - Only ssh (22) and https (443) are permitted. Telnet and http are not: to allow them, add the same
            line with '--dport 23' or '--dport 80' for each address above, before the DROP.
          - The udp 161 lines are the SNMP client restriction of Step 6, unless the unit has an SNMP
            access menu of its own (then enter the same clients there).
          - ICMP (ping): the last lines accept it from the same networks, on eth0 only. The unit's own
            'Ping Access' item (/N, item 30; Limited by default) is separate and not changed by this list.
          - IPv4 only: the unit's 'iptables', not 'ip6tables'. An IPv6 entry of the lists is skipped, with a note.
          - The unit holds 48 entries (12 to a page): this list has 11; with the DROP, the
            OUTPUT ACCEPT and the three policies of the last step, 16. A command is 256 characters at most.

        This line turns the list into a restriction, and it is the one that can lock you out. The
        walkthrough does not apply it: you paste it, last, yourself, once the steps above work.
          a) Keep the serial session of Step 1 open (and a second session ready). It is the way back.
          b) Add the DROP as the LAST line of the IP Tables list (after line 11):
               12. iptables -A INPUT -j DROP
             or paste the whole list again, with the DROP in it, in one go. The block below is the rules of
             Step 5, then the DROP, the OUTPUT ACCEPT and the three policies, LAST (the order a lab unit
             took without cutting the pasting session off). The paste replaces every entry, and the unit
             applies it at once, so the test of c) runs with the DROP already in force.

<iptables>
iptables -A INPUT -i lo -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -m conntrack --ctstate ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -p tcp -s 10.0.0.42/32 --dport 22 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -p tcp -s 10.0.0.42/32 --dport 443 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -p tcp -s 192.0.2.0/24 --dport 22 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -p tcp -s 192.0.2.0/24 --dport 443 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -p udp -s 10.0.0.42/32 --dport 161 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -p udp -s 203.0.113.0/24 --dport 161 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -i eth0 -s 10.0.0.42/32 -p icmp -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -i eth0 -s 192.0.2.0/24 -p icmp -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -i eth0 -s 203.0.113.0/24 -p icmp -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -j DROP
iptables -A OUTPUT -j ACCEPT
iptables -P INPUT DROP
iptables -P OUTPUT DROP
iptables -P FORWARD DROP
</iptables>

          c) Before saving, test a login from a permitted address (repeat Step 8, and from the tacctl
             server: tacctl scope snmp lab test <unit-address>). A login from an address
             outside the list must now be refused.
          d) Save only when the test works (any session that leaves a top-level menu saves the whole
             configuration). If it fails, delete line 12 on the serial session first; after the paste of
             the block, clear the three policies as well (below).
        The unit has no commit-confirm and no rollback: the way back is clearing the slots (<SPACE><CR> at a
        slot's prompt; after the paste of the block the DROP is entry 12 and the three policies are
        entries 14 to 16), or pasting the block of Step 5 again, from the serial session.
